scenario: A climate-reporting platform logs only manufacturing plants with annual emissions above 500 tons because lower-emission facilities are exempt from mandatory filing. A policy analyst wants the mean emissions across all plants in the sector.

data.description: Only plants above 500 tons are observed. Emissions are modeled as Normal with known standard deviation sigma = 180 tons.

question: Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean annual emissions mu across all plants and (b) the fraction of plants that appear in the reporting platform.
naive_answer: Average sector emissions are about 602 tons because that is the mean among reported plants.
naive_trap: The filing threshold excludes the lower-emission majority of plants. The observed mean is an upper-tail mean, not the sector-wide average.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: Solve 602.13 = mu + 180*lambda((500-mu)/180). Step 2: The solution has alpha about 0.8, implying mu = 500 - 0.8*180 = 356. Step 3: The reporting fraction is sf(0.8) about 0.2119.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(500-mu)/180
    return mu + 180*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a) - 602.13
mu=brentq(eq,-1000,499.99)
frac=norm.sf((500-mu)/180)
assert abs(mu-356)<6 and abs(frac-0.2119)<0.005
